old: This report presents a framework for deploying and maintaining deep-learning (DL) surrogate models as reliable decision-support tools for long-term groundwater remediation within the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Environmental Management (EM) complex. DL surrogates can accelerate predictions of groundwater flow and transport by factors of 103 to 105 relative to physics-based numerical simulators, making it feasible to evaluate large scenario sets, explore uncertainty, and support planning decisions that would otherwise be computationally impractical. However, surrogates trained at a single point in time may lose accuracy as site conditions evolve, remediation systems are modified, conceptual models are refined, or new field data reveal behavior outside the original training domain. Without a systematic process for detecting and correcting such degradation, surrogate-based decision support may become unreliable, which is unacceptable in compliance-driven settings governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) and DOE EM-QA-001 quality assurance requirements.

old: The physical phenomena represented typically include advection and dispersion of dissolved species, sorption onto solid phases, and associated reaction processes (Genuchten 2016; Sethi and Di Molfetta 2019), and non-Fickian plume spreading arising from heterogeneity and diffusion-controlled mass exchange between transmissive and low-permeability zones (Guo et al. 2021). Density-driven flow occurs in systems impacted by dense nonaqueous phase liquid / light nonaqueous phase liquid (Huling 1991; McCaulou 1995; Newell 1995) or by seawater intrusion (Werner et al. 2013; Xu et al. 2019). old: Convolutional encoder-decoder architectures such as U-Net and residual network variants treat spatial fields as images and learn direct mappings from input fields, including hydraulic conductivity, boundary conditions, and pumping patterns, to output fields such as hydraulic heads, salinity distributions, and plume extents. Convolutions preserve interfaces, sharp fronts, and channelized structures, making these networks well suited for high-resolution spatial prediction. Representative applications include attention U-Net architectures for steady-state hydraulic head fields (Taccari et al. 2022), image-to-image regression for multiphase flow (Mo et al. 2019), autoregressive residual U-Net for dynamic multiphase flow and solute transport (Jiang et al. 2021), and U-Net surrogates for transient groundwater flow inverse problems (Lauzon 2024) and P&T optimization (Song et al. 2025).

old: Across the five families, several training practices recur in literature. Training datasets are generated by sampling parameter and boundary condition ranges, commonly using Latin hypercube or quasi-random designs, and running the corresponding high-fidelity simulations to produce input-output pairs (Asher et al. 2015; Razavi et al. 2012). The number of simulations required varies by problem complexity and surrogate architecture but generally falls in the range of hundreds to low thousands of realizations (Mo et al. 2019; Wen et al. 2022; Zhu and Zabaras 2018). Input fields that span orders of magnitude, such as hydraulic conductivity, are typically log-transformed prior to training (Tang et al. 2020), and all features are standardized to stabilize optimization and ensure consistent inference (Mo et al. 2019). Hold-out realizations spanning distinct parameter ranges or time windows are reserved for testing to guard against overfitting (Jiang et al. 2025; Wen et al. 2022).
